items.followUp: State the main feature of Dobereiner’s triads and give one example.

rubric.why: Identifies the triad as three elements with similar properties.
rubric.description: Three elements with similar chemical properties
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a triad consists of three elements with similar properties.

rubric.why: States the relationship between the atomic masses in a triad.
rubric.description: Middle element’s atomic mass is approximately the mean of the other two
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the approximate arithmetic-mean relationship.

modelAnswer: Dobereiner arranged some elements in groups of three, called triads, whose elements had similar chemical properties.
The atomic mass of the middle element was approximately the arithmetic mean of the atomic masses of the other two elements. Example: Li, Na and K.

items.followUp: Explain why atomic size decreases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Recognizes the increasing number of occupied shells down a group.
rubric.description: An additional electron shell is added down a group
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each successive element down a group has an additional occupied shell.

rubric.why: Connects the added shell and shielding to the greater distance of the outer electrons from the nucleus.
rubric.description: Outer electrons are farther from the nucleus, so atomic radius increases
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the outer electrons are farther from the nucleus (or that increased shielding reduces the nuclear attraction on them).

modelAnswer: Down a group, each successive element has an additional occupied electron shell.
Therefore, the outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus and the atomic radius increases.

items.followUp: Identify the type of covalent bond in O₂ and N₂.

rubric.why: Identifies the bonding in methane correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the C–H bonds in CH₄ as single covalent bonds.

rubric.why: Identifies the bonding in ethane correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the C–C and C–H bonds in C₂H₆ as single covalent bonds.

modelAnswer: CH₄: It contains four single covalent C–H bonds.
C₂H₆: It contains a single covalent C–C bond and single covalent C–H bonds.

items.followUp: Write two properties of a suspension.

rubric.why: Gives a defining property of a solution.
rubric.description: A solution is a homogeneous mixture
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a solution is homogeneous or uniform throughout.

rubric.why: Gives another valid property of a solution.
rubric.description: Solution particles remain dispersed and do not settle
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid property such as stability, particles not settling, or inability to separate the solute by ordinary filtration.

modelAnswer: A solution is a homogeneous mixture with uniform composition throughout.
Its particles do not settle on standing, so the solution is stable.

items.followUp: Name two metals that are highly reactive.

rubric.why: Names one of the least reactive metals.
Names another of the least reactive metals.

modelAnswer: Gold and platinum are two of the least reactive metals.

rubric.why: States what happens to electrons for an electropositive atom.
rubric.description: Tendency to lose or donate electrons
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an atom tends to lose, donate or release electrons.

rubric.why: States the result of losing electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that losing electrons forms a positive ion or cation.

modelAnswer: Electropositive character is the tendency of an atom to lose or donate electrons.
By losing electrons, the atom forms a positive ion (cation).

items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for chlorine reacting with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide.

rubric.why: Identifies the products of chlorine reacting with hot, concentrated sodium hydroxide.
rubric.description: Products are sodium chloride, sodium chlorate and water
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving all three products: NaCl, NaClO₃ and H₂O.

rubric.why: Gives the balanced equation under the stated conditions.
rubric.description: Balanced equation with hot, concentrated NaOH
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation and the hot, concentrated conditions.

items.followUp: Name the isotopes of hydrogen and write the nuclear fusion reaction between deuterium and tritium.

rubric.why: States the number of hydrogen isotopes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that hydrogen has three isotopes.

rubric.why: Names or identifies the three isotopes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming or identifying all three isotopes.

rubric.why: Identifies deuterium and tritium as fuels for fusion power generation.
rubric.description: Deuterium and tritium are used as fusion fuels
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that deuterium and tritium are used in nuclear fusion for power generation.

rubric.why: Identifies the products of the deuterium–tritium fusion reaction.
rubric.description: Fusion produces helium and a neutron
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying helium and a neutron as products.

rubric.why: States that fusion releases energy, which can be used to generate power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the reaction releases energy.

modelAnswer: Hydrogen has three isotopes: protium (¹₁H), deuterium (²₁H) and tritium (³₁H).
Deuterium and tritium can be used as fuels for nuclear fusion to generate power.
The fusion reaction produces helium and a neutron and releases a large amount of energy.
